title: Cross-origin iframe: review manually
user_impact: Embedded content (maps, videos, consent widgets) may be inaccessible to screen reader users.
technical_impact: Iframe content is unreachable via CDP — automatic rule checking is not possible.
source: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 (and every SC for embedded content); axe-core frame-tested; HTML §7.1 origin
applicability: Every perceivable <iframe>/<frame> (not hidden, aria-hidden, role none/presentation, display:none, visibility:hidden, or 1px or smaller) in the document, its shadow roots included.
expectation:
One UNTESTED note per perceivable frame whose document is cross-origin to the
page, located at the frame. Same-origin and srcdoc frames, and frames that are
not perceivable (hidden, aria-hidden, display:none, at most 1px in either
dimension), get no note. A frame inserted by script or inside a shadow root is
part of the page and is judged the same way. Never a pass or a violation.
manual_reason:
The rule only flags embedded content from another origin for a human: whether
that content meets WCAG is outside the page's own markup and is never
concluded automatically.
